codeReview.summary: The fix resolves part of the original scrutiny feedback: artifact upload now returns a 202 operation envelope, the operation-envelope table now includes both upload routes, and deployment deletion now attempts a runtime stop. However, the feature still does not fully close the blocking findings because uploaded-artifact operation results still omit buildStrategy=prebuilt_wasm and the new deployment tests remain stubbed rather than proving real runtime lifecycle behavior.

issues.description: CreateUploadedArtifactBuild now persists StrategyPrebuiltWasm to the database, but the returned BuildJob struct still never sets BuildStrategy. buildWorkflowGrain.handleArtifactUpload returns that in-memory BuildJob directly as the operation result (backend/janus-api/internal/actors/grains.go:435), so polling a successful artifact-upload operation still omits the required buildStrategy="prebuilt_wasm" payload. The new handler test stubs hardcode BuildStrategy on their fake CreateUploadedArtifactBuild responses, which masks the production gap instead of verifying it.

The new deployment coverage still does not verify the real end-to-end runtime lifecycle required by the original failure. TestDeploymentOperationPoll_RunningWithRuntimeEndpoint seeds store.operations with a pre-succeeded result instead of creating and polling a deployment, and TestDeploymentDelete_StatusBecomesStoppedAfterOperation only calls the stub store after DELETE; that stub DeleteDeployment implementation (lines 63-70) just flips status and never exercises core.State.DeleteDeployment or runtime.Stop. The suite still never performs an HTTP GET against a live runtimeEndpoint for a 2xx response, nor proves that the runtime becomes unreachable after deletion.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill still says API changes require manual curl.exe verification recorded in interactiveChecks, but this fix handoff again records only automated commands while marking followedProcedure=true. That makes the procedure signal unreliable for backend API/runtime work.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared e2e-pipeline notes still under-enumerate async mutation routes after this fix: they mention source-bundle uploads but not artifact uploads, even though ArtifactUploadRoute now also participates in the operation-envelope contract. That omission can cause future reviewers/workers to undercount required coverage again.

summary: Fix review failed. The patch does resolve the original 202-envelope gap for artifact uploads and adds the previously missing upload routes to the operation-envelope suite, but it still leaves one deployment-access blocker unresolved in production (artifact-upload results omit buildStrategy prebuilt_wasm) and does not add the real runtime-access/shutdown verification that the prior deployment review required.
